*.why: Rules for every projection case. (1) Ids and times: a `binds` token on a create is bound to the id Core answers (same prefix, a v4 uuid); any other `<id:n>` the replay meets first in Core's rows (a repo, project, connection or saved query a link, import or sync makes) matches any id with that prefix and a v4 uuid, the same one everywhere in the case; `<core:n>` in `changes.json` is a row only Core makes, matched the same way; `<now>` is any time the Executor gave; seeded ids and times stay. (2) Files: a query, dashboard or template file carries its stable id once Core has written it (Q22: `id: <uuid>` as the first frontmatter or YAML line, `"id"` as the first key of a dashboard's JSON; `project.yaml` and `labels.yaml` have none). Core writes the id when it writes the file for a real change, and keeps the one the file had; it never rewrites a file only to add an id, so a file Core didn't write is byte-identical to the recording. The replay checks a written file's id is a v4 uuid kept for the file's whole life (renames included), removes that line or key, and compares the rest byte for byte. Paths are absolute on the recorder's disk; the replay roots them in its temp directory. Directories aren't compared. An import of shared projects writes no file (`import/missing-project-yaml`); a sync writes only the files the rule table says. (3) Hashes (Decision 34): a file's hash is SHA-256 of `write(parse(text))` and a row's of `write(parse(write(row)))`, where `write` is Core's canonical writer for the kind's content (without the id, and for a dashboard without the viewport, Q24) and `parse` its reader. So a row and the file Core wrote for it always hash the same, whatever line endings or edge whitespace the row holds (`queries/trailing-whitespace-and-crlf`, `write-query/crlf-body`). (4) Invariants, checked after every step. (a) Every row linked to a file (a non-NULL `shared_path` for a query or dashboard, or the path in a connection's `shared_connection_id`) whose file exists, wasn't skipped (Decision 32) and isn't in a repo with conflicted files has `shared_base` = that file's hash and `shared_file_id` = the file's id (NULL when it has none), unless a value was withheld: a sync update from a file whose name another row holds keeps the row's name (Task 4b review, flag 4), and then `shared_base` is the row's own hash, which differs from the file's only by that name. A NULL `shared_path` is not a link. The share toggle stores the link even when the template write fails: the base stays unset, so the next sync writes the file. (b) After a step whose `core` calls all succeeded (a call that answers `projection.status: failed` succeeded), every shared query and dashboard, and every explicitly shared connection (one that has a `shared_connection_id`; Decision 53), in a linked project whose directory is stored (`projects.shared_dir`; Core stores it at the project's first sync, link or import) has a non-NULL path (`shared_path`, or for a connection `shared_connection_id`), except the rows the step's `pathless` list names. Nothing else is exempt. A name-only change from a teammate merges with a local content change: when the base is the file under the row's name (F′) and the row changed, the file takes the row's content under the teammate's name and the next sync gives the row that name, with no conflict and no version (coordinator's decision). (5) Rows: the 0004 link columns (`projects.shared_dir`, `*.shared_path`, `*.shared_base`, `*.shared_file_id`) are dropped from the dump before comparing, after (4) and the step's `links`. `shared_repos` rows compare `id`, `path` and `name` (Decision 43), and their `data` follows from the case's repo calls: a repo call is `shared.linkProject`, `shared.unlinkProject`, `shared.importProjects`, `shared.repoRegister`, `shared.repoUpdate`, `shared.repoRemove`, `git.pull` and `git.push`. A seeded repo that no repo call names keeps its `data` byte for byte. One that only `git.pull` or `git.push` named keeps it byte for byte except `lastSyncAt`, which is a time (Core's pull and push write it on success, spliced into the stored JSON; Decision 43). `app_state` isn't in any expected `rows`: `activeRepoId` keeps its seeded value (absent when the seed has none) in every step (Decision 42), whatever the recording shows. Expected rows hold only what the step's Core calls write: a `projectSidebarSet` the page made on its own, in a step whose `core` doesn't send it, isn't in them. (6) Notices: a step whose `core` holds a `shared` call gives exactly the `notices` its entry lists, as a set, and none when it lists none. Each file is named at most once per session, whatever the notice. `projection` and `outcome` are compared only where listed (only the fields given).

queries/renamed-in-the-repo-keeps-its-id.why: Q22 A (Decision 34): pairing goes by id first. Step 0 pairs the file by name (the row has no link yet) and records its path and id. The first pull's file has the same id under a new path and name: the row follows (its name and `shared_path`), with no new row and no `removedInRepo`. The second pull's file (an older release's rewrite) has no id: pairing falls back to the stored path, the row takes the new text with a version, and `shared_file_id` is cleared, since the file has none (Core writes it again at its next real write of the file, never just to add it). The third pull moves the file: no id, the stored path is gone, so pairing falls back to the name. Steps 1 to 5 (Task 4b review correction): the row takes the file's whole content, so `tags` is the file's `[]`, as in every other update from a file.

queries/trailing-whitespace-and-crlf.why: Decisions 34 and 45: Core writes the file once, with `\n` line endings (the body's `\r\n` too). The row and the file hash the same (`write(parse(write(row)))` against `write(parse(text))`), so the next syncs change nothing: no version, no notice.

repo/two-projects-one-repo-pull.why: Decision 35 (bug 12): "Ops" was activated once before the pull, so both queries have a base and the pull is `R = B, F ≠ B` for each. The pull is followed by a sync of every project linked to the repo, so both take their files (each with a version) at once, with no notice, and the activations change nothing. The pull also sets the repo's `lastSyncAt` (Core's pull writes it, spliced into the stored row; Decision 43).

dashboards/long-cjk-names-collide.why: Q21 (Decision 39): the stem is cut at a character boundary to 250 bytes (83 characters, 249 bytes), so the first file is 254 bytes with `.json`. The second has the same stem; its `-2` suffix would take the name to 256 bytes, so `free_path` cuts the stem again (82 characters) to fit 255.

queries/nfd-name-from-a-macos-teammate.why: Q21 (Decision 39): the stem is `ärger` (NFC). `free_path` compares names case-insensitively and after NFC, as APFS and NTFS treat them, so the NFD `ärger.sql` takes the name and the new file is `ärger-2.sql`. The teammate's file keeps its NFD name (Core never renames an existing file).

unlink/repo-still-used.why: Decision 40: unlinking forgets the repo only when no project uses it. "Ops" still does, so the repo row stays (byte for byte) and "Ops" keeps syncing. Q31 (owner, 2026-10-01): unlinking keeps the user's own connections (shared from here, `shared_origin` `exported`) unlinked and local-only with their secrets, and removes the ones the repo brought only when the call says so. The recorded call has no `removeImported`: the recording's GUI removed the template connections, which is the user confirming, so the replays send `removeImported: true` for it. The seeded connection's link has no origin (an older release stored it), which counts as imported, so the expected rows are unchanged (see the README's Corrections).

connections/never-shared-in-a-linked-pro.why: Decision 53: a connection reaches the repo only when it is explicitly shared (it has a link, or the user shared it). One that merely isn't local-only is treated as local: the edit publishes nothing, no sync writes a template for it, and it stays unlinked.

link/unticked-connection-stays-local.why: Q30 (Decisions 40 and 53): only the ticked connection is exported and linked. "Billing" was left unticked, so no template is written for it and it stays local (unlinked); the settings save imports nothing; and editing it later publishes nothing, since it was never explicitly shared.
